articles.title: Apple Released the iPhone X Nine Years Ago Today
articles.content: Apple's iPhone X went on sale nine years ago today, November 3, 2017. The 10th-anniversary iPhone was the first with an all-screen OLED display and no Home button, and its gesture navigation and Face ID authentication shaped the flagship iPhone models that followed it. Announced on September 12, 2017 , the iPhone X used its TrueDepth camera to introduce Face ID, which replaced Touch ID on the device. Powered by the A11 Bionic chip, it was also Apple's first iPhone to start at $999. Apple classified the device as vintage in 2024 . Recently, Touch ID made an unlikely return to iPhones with the iPhone Duo. Apple is expected to introduce a redesigned 20th-anniversary iPhone in late 2027. This article, " Apple Released the iPhone X Nine Years Ago Today " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums
articles.author: Tim Hardwick

articles.title: YouTube’s dreaded Server Error 400 is back to haunt Android users
articles.content: TL;DR YouTube has acknowledged that some Android users are still encountering Server Error 400, despite announcing a fix on November 1. The error prevents affected users from accessing YouTube or loading videos normally. Google is working on another fix, but its suggested workarounds will delete downloaded videos. YouTube declared victory over a frustrating Android bug over the weekend, only to find itself fighting the same battle two days later. The company has walked back its all-clear on the dreaded Server Error 400, confirming that some users still can’t access the app or watch videos normally. In a fresh update to its official support thread , Google acknowledged the problem persists and that its teams are still working on a fix. Google hasn’t provided a revised timeline for when affected users can expect relief.
articles.author: Hillary Keverenge

articles.title: Nudify apps are hiding in plain sight on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store
articles.content: TL;DR Researchers uncovered a network of over 400 ‘nudify’ apps and websites on the Play Store and App Store. These apps masquerade as innocent tools and reveal a hidden deepfake interface after installation. The apps were traced back to Chinese developers and Hong Kong-based KeLing Technology Limited. Apple and Google often talk about the strict guidelines that apps need to follow in order to be allowed on their stores. However, every few months, new reports emerge of harmful apps making their way onto both the Play Store and the App Store. Apps like the fake Chrome browser spotted last month are concerning enough, but Google and Apple have a much bigger, more alarming problem on their hands with “nudify” apps. Earlier this year, around 38 “nudify” apps were found on the App Store and Play Store , accounting for a combined 483 million downloads and $122 million in revenue. Now, Wired has uncovered that there may be several hundred more. What’s worse is that they are now masquerading as innocent services, such as language tutoring, AI-based pet photo editing, and workout coaching apps.
articles.author: Akshay Gangwar
articles.fingerprint: app apple apps google hiding nudify plain play sight store

articles.title: The espresso machine I recommend to all beginners is $200 off right now — the same price as Black Friday
articles.content: I've tested well over 50 coffee machines now. Manuals, bean-to-cups, superautomatics — even the lever Flair 49 Pro (yes, no electricity involved at all). But which is the ultimate best espresso machine... for beginners? I would recommend something with a built-in grinder. While some people will tell you machines with built-in grinders are inherently inferior, I disagree. A "good" grinder can set you back hundreds of dollars — on top of your espresso machine. This can easily make your coffee setup almost a thousand dollars... and that's before the actual coffee beans. So if you want your first espresso machine but you're not sure which one to get, let me help you out. I'd recommend the Breville Barista Express , which we awarded 4.5 stars in our review, and it remains a classic. And the best part? It's currently just $499 at Amazon — yes, the same price as the Breville Bambino Plus . So you're really getting that grinder for free. The Barista Express remains one of the most popular and recommended espresso machines for a reason. Like every other Breville, it has a PID controller (although unadjustable, but better than no PID controller!), a powerful steam wand, and a built in grinder. View Deal Why is the Breville Barista Express so good for beginners? (Image credit: Tom's Guide) One reason: convenience. The Breville Barista Express is easy to use, making it ideal for newer home baristas. While you still need to dial in beans yourself, this is a skill all baristas should dedicate time to learning — and you'll notice your espresso tastes so much better once you've figured it out. Your espresso should pour like honey . Like every other Breville, the Barista Express has a PID controller, which means the machine controls your water temperature at every stage of the brewing process. I would personally never buy an espresso machine without a PID controller (or similar). This ensures your espresso is never burned or weak, but just right. You can also customize pre-infusion time: this is where you soak the grounds with water at low pressure, extracting nuanced and delicate flavors, before ramping up the pressure for a full extraction. But you also don't have to use this feature — you can just press the "shot" button and espresso will come out. So while the Breville Barista Express has a range of enthusiast features like adjustable pre-infusion and a PID controller, it also has a built-in grinder and easy-to-use steam wand. This machine will grow with you, from your early days of Googling things like: "What is espresso???" all the way to your serious barista era. It's the Goldilocks of coffee, so to speak. And because the Bambino Plus is $499 full price, you're kind of getting the built-in Baratza grinder for free. articles.title: Creating your own avatar in Google Vids just got a lot easier
articles.content: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Google Vids now lets you create custom avatars using just photos. Previously, you could only choose from predefined characters or use your own AI avatar generated through a long process in Gemini. The new option makes it as simple as uploading an image, which it processes and enhances itself. Google Vids is a video editing platform part of the Workspace suite of apps. While you can just edit videos on a typical timeline, Gemini adds a lot more features, including the options to turn Docs or Slides into videos , edit videos with simple text-based prompts , and even transform how people in the videos look. Besides video editing, Vids also lets you generate human-looking (or human-inspired) characters using AI , with options to customize characteristics such as age, gender, race, and more. Now, Google is adding more options to customize the avatar and make it resemble you. Google is now adding an option in the Vids app that lets you create custom avatars using just images. articles.title: Forget retraining - AI can now tweak another AI's weights
articles.content: The outputs of AI models are the result of a complex interplay between neurons, weights, training, and inference, and are therefore difficult to follow. But in some ways they're starting to look more like open books. Recent work by Anthropic safety fellow Joshua Fonseca Rivera has revealed how certain neurons in a neural network can be associated with a specific persona . Now, computer scientists from MIT's Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) have found that frontier AI models like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can rewrite the weights of another model directly, as opposed to indirectly through training, and alter their behavior. "We find early signs that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading, writing, and reasoning about neural network weights," said Rikiya Takehi, a PhD student at MIT CSAIL, in a social media post . "Instead of training, models may treat raw weights like readable, editable code: diagnosing failures and patching them directly." To demonstrate that, Takehi and colleagues Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to make it better at math. Astra changed only 0.016 percent of the model's weights, reducing its reasoning loops and improving its math performance by as much as sixfold on the MATH-500 benchmark, while boosting its instruction-following score on the IFEval benchmark roughly threefold. There was no training using gradient descent ; Astra just revised the numerical values that constitute Qwen's weights. "All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops," the researchers wrote in a blog post . "It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming. "Throughout the history of deep learning, we encoded our simplistic inductive biases into tiny symbolic optimizers like Adam or Muon. This is changing: our neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about their weights." Astra's ability to program weights extends to being able to write a neural network from scratch, zero-shot. The researchers told Astra: "write, from scratch, the weights of a policy network that plays [Breakout] as well as possible." And it did so. Takehi suggests this technique shows promise for improving models without the consequences of catastrophic forgetting , which can occur when a model is revised to include new knowledge. More generally, the authors expect Weight-Space Programming will open the door to new ways to understand models and optimize them, and to implement recursive self-improvement. The technique may also prove useful for reducing model sycophancy and improving interpretability and alignment. The next step, the authors say, involves building a benchmark and a harness for carrying out Weight-Space Programming on LLMs. "We believe this will provide a standardized evaluation to measure and accelerate progress in Weight-Space Programming, turning what currently seems like black magic into a rigorous, reproducible engineering discipline," they say. ®

articles.title: Real people at AI companies may be reading your private chats — here's how to protect yourself
articles.content: You might tell ChatGPT things you’d never share with a stranger. Maybe you’ve asked it about a medical concern, argued with your spouse in a conversation about relationship advice or uploaded a document containing financial information. But before your next conversation, here's something to know: Real people at AI companies may be able to read some of what you share. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic all have policies that allow certain conversations to be reviewed by humans, whether to improve their AI systems, investigate potential safety violations or troubleshoot problems. That doesn’t mean someone is sitting behind a screen reading every message you send, but the assumption that your AI conversations are strictly between you and the chatbot is not accurate. Not to mention, just deleting a conversation doesn’t always mean the company deletes every copy immediately. In Google’s case, Gemini chats reviewed by humans can remain in company systems for up to three years, even after you delete your activity. Here’s what actually happens to your conversations, who might be able to read them and what you can do to protect your privacy. Yes, humans can read some AI conversations (Image credit: Getty Images/Kelly Sikkema) When you type a question into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, your message is typically sent to the company’s servers, where an AI model processes it and generates a response. Most of that process is automated. But AI companies also use human reviewers to evaluate certain conversations. Several reasons might prompt a review; safety is a big one. AI companies use automated systems to detect potentially harmful requests, policy violations and suspicious activity. Some interactions may be escalated for human review. Another reason conversations are reviewed is for improving the AI itself. Depending on your settings and the company’s policies, selected conversations may be used to evaluate responses, identify mistakes and help improve future models. Companies generally describe measures intended to protect users during these reviews, including limiting access and removing identifying information. But removing a person’s name or account details doesn’t necessarily remove every sensitive fact contained in a conversation. For example, a chat about a medical diagnosis , workplace dispute or financial problem could contain personal information even without the user’s name attached. The important difference is that human review doesn’t happen to every conversation, and the rules vary depending on which chatbot you’re using. What big tech might do with your conversations ChatGPT (Image credit: Shutterstock) OpenAI allows consumer ChatGPT conversations to be used to improve its models unless users opt out. You can disable this by opening Settings > Data Controls and turning off Improve the model for everyone . But disabling training doesn’t mean every conversation becomes inaccessible to human reviewers. OpenAI’s Data Controls FAQ explains that Temporary Chats aren’t used for training but may be reviewed to monitor abuse. Temporary Chats also don’t appear in your regular chat history and are generally deleted from OpenAI’s systems after 30 days. For ordinary saved conversations, OpenAI says deleting a chat removes it from your account immediately and schedules it for permanent deletion within 30 days, unless the information has already been de-identified or must be retained for legal or security reasons. Google Gemini (Image credit: Shutterstock) Google is particularly explicit about how human reviewers may access conversations. According to Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub , some conversations are reviewed by humans to improve its services and help protect users. Google says conversations sent to service providers for review are disconnected from users’ accounts before being examined. But there’s a significant catch: Chats reviewed by humans can be retained for up to three years, and deleting your Gemini Apps activity…

articles.content: TL;DR Snapseed v4.2 is gradually rolling out on Android and iOS. The update adds support for importing presets and LUTs, sharing custom Looks with their LUTs, browsing community Looks, and a depth-based mode for Lens Blur. It also brings the Motion Blur tool from iPhone to Android, along with full multi-wheel Color Grading. As a longtime Snapseed fan, I was stoked when Google finally started showing the app some love this year. Since then, the company has rolled out several new features and improved the app in multiple ways. Well, it doesn’t seem like Google is planning to stop anytime soon. Google has started rolling out Snapseed v4.2 on Android and iOS, and the update introduces several new features to the much-loved photo-editing app (via Droid Life ). The update brings the Motion Blur tool—previously only available on iPhones—to Android users as well.

articles.title: Ridley Scott’s $100M box office flop might secretly be his best movie — and you can stream it free on Tubi
articles.content: Get people to name Ridley Scott’s best movie and you’ll hear “Gladiator,” “Alien” or “Blade Runner,” but one of his finest in recent years is a film almost nobody saw in theaters. That movie is “The Last Duel,” a brutal, brilliant medieval drama from 2021 that flopped hard on release, but is getting its second wind on streaming thanks to platforms like Tubi. Directed by Scott and based on Eric Jager’s book, “The Last Duel” dramatizes the true story of the last legally sanctioned duel to the death in medieval France. It tells the same events three times, “Rashomon”-style, from three different points of view, with the final version belonging to the woman at the center of it all. It pulled in just $30 million at the box office against a $100 million budget, but critics admired it, and in the years since it’s come to be regarded as one of Scott’s best films. Now that it's streaming free on Tubi, there's no excuse not to give one of the most underrated movies of the decade the attention it always deserved. What is 'The Last Duel' about? J ean de Carrouges (Matt Damon) and Jacques Le Gris (Adam Driver) are close friends in 14th-century France, two men who once fought side by side in battle. But they couldn’t be more different. Carrouges is a proud, hot-tempered knight who feels the world owes him more than it’s given him, while Le Gris is charming, educated and quick to rise in the favor of their powerful lord, Count Pierre d’Alençon (Ben Affleck). As Le Gris climbs and Carrouges keeps getting passed over for lands and titles he believes are rightfully his, their friendship devolves into a rivalry. Things escalate further when Carrouges marries Marguerite (Jodie Comer), a strong-willed noblewoman. While Carrouges is away, Le Gris forces his way into their home and assaults her. When her husband returns, Marguerite does something extraordinarily dangerous for a woman of her time: She refuses to stay silent, naming Le Gris as her attacker. Enraged and determined to defend his wife’s honor, Carrouges petitions the king for a trial by combat, a duel to the death in which God is said to grant victory to whoever is telling the truth. Why I recommend streaming 'The Last Duel' "The Last Duel" is an interesting mix of both rage and spectacle. I went in expecting a straightforward medieval epic, so I was surprised to realize it had a lot to say about truth and power dynamics — and, of course, believing women at its heart. (Image credit: Tubi) As a "Rashomon" fan, the movie's three-perspective structure is what actually elevates it. Watching the exact same events replay from Jean’s self-serving point of view, then Jacques’s, then Marguerite’s, you start to notice how casually these men rewrite their own histories, and how differently a woman experiences the same moments the men barely register. Matt Damon and Adam Driver are both excellent as the two rivals, Ben Affleck is a surprising addition I didn't see coming, and Jodie Comer is fantastic as Marguerite. And in the end, the final duel is one of the most viscerally intense sequences Scott has ever put to film. If you're wondering about how it might leave you mentally when the credits roll, you can just sit with it at home to reckon with those feelings. Whatever the case, you should absolutely give it a watch, as you'll want to make sure you catch it while it's streaming free. Stream "The Last Duel" free on Tubi now

That’s cheaper than AT&T’s $125 standalone 5Gbps rate announced earlier this year, and even its $100 bundled price. T-Mobile doesn’t require a wireless subscription to qualify.

articles.title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
articles.content: Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge. Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used. Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own. Agentic AI for Cities From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough. In Spain, 1MillionBot combines open source ALIA models trained at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with NVIDIA Nemotron and other models in resident-service agents for Madrid Digital (Comunidad de Madrid), Administració Oberta de Catalunya and 150+ deployments across Spain, handling municipal procedures, appointment requests, urban-planning incidents and service inquiries. In the San Francisco Bay Area , LiveX is bringing its AI City vision to life with NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Nemotron open models, and Omniverse and Metropolis libraries on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs. The interactive, conversational AI hosts understand people’s needs, provide answers and take action, and can be tailored to local languages and service needs in airports, hospitals, local events and other public spaces. Vision AI agents can turn existing city camera feeds into operational insights, helping teams identify mobility and safety issues and coordinate emergency responses across city services. In Wrocław, Poland , K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions. In Malaysia , ITMAX bundles infrastructure and agentic AI applications into long-term managed services for cities, including for traffic management. Built with reference to Cosmos, Nemotron and the Metropolis VSS blueprint, ITMAX’s SamurAI V2 vision agents are scaling on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to support 17,000+ cameras by 2027. ITMAX integrates TeraSim, an open source traffic simulation platform from Laplace Intelligence, to test signal timing, reducing peak-hour corridor travel times by up to 26%. Plan and Operate Critical Infrastructure With Digital Twins Beyond public-facing services, digital twins can help cities expedite infrastructure planning, minimizing disruption to local communities. City digital twins can also serve as a real-time operational simulation to facilitate faster decision-making. At Dangote’s Lekki refinery in Nigeria, Honeywell Technologies’ Forge Plant Cognition uses Nemotron-powered AI agents to understand operational data. A digital twin of the plant and its processes, built using Omniverse libraries, is also planned to support simulation and training. The platform, built on Dell PowerEdge servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO accelerators, helps operators identify bottlenecks, anticipate equipment and process issues, and optimize plant performance. In Taiwan , Linker Vision and Dutch architecture firm MVRDV are using NVIDIA Omniverse and Nemotron to build environmental, social and governance agents that can assess the environmental impact of various urban planning…

articles.title: How to spot an abandoned rabbit's nest in your lawn — and clear it out safely
articles.content: After an unusually warm fall, many yards are still showing signs of late-season wildlife activity. Extended mild weather encourages wild rabbits to breed later into the year than usual, meaning shallow nests that typically appear in mid-spring can linger well into the cooler months. As you head out for late-season garden tidy-ups, raking leaves or giving the grass a final cut can easily unearth a suspicious depression in the turf. Before running the mower across it or filling it in, a quick check ensures the young have safely vacated the nest and that your lawn can be tidied without disturbing any remaining kits. 1. How to recognise a rabbit’s nest (Image: © Shutterstock) Most people picture rabbits living in deep underground tunnels, but garden rabbits actually raise their babies right on the surface. Instead of digging down, a mother rabbit scrapes out a shallow, bowl-shaped dip in the grass, tucked under a bush, or even sitting out in the open lawn. To hide the spot from predators, she covers the hollow with a blanket of dried grass, dead leaves, and plucked fur. Because the nest sits completely level with the rest of the lawn, it looks just like an ordinary patch of dead grass until you step closer and notice the woven fur and bedding on top. 2. Confirm the nest is completely empty (Image: © Shutterstock) Now that temperatures have dropped and we're into the colder stretch of fall, any late-season litters should have already moved on. If the grass cover has caved in, feels cold to the touch, is blowing apart in the wind, and shows no signs of wriggling underneath , the nest has been abandoned. If you want to be completely sure before touching it, place two small twigs in an "X" over the top and leave them overnight. If the twigs are still sitting in the exact same spot the next morning, you can safely assume the nest is empty. 3. Clear the bedding and repair your lawn (Image: © Shutterstock) Once you know the nest is empty, clearing it away takes just a couple of minutes and stops pests from taking up residence in the leftover bedding. Slip on a pair of garden gloves and lift the clump of fur, leaves, and dried grass out of the dip. If you are worried about lingering fleas or mites, use a garden trowel to scoop out the top layer of underlying soil along with the bedding. Seal the material in a bag and toss it straight into your garden waste bin . Finally, level out the dip by filling it with a simple mix of topsoil and sand . Press it down firmly with your foot so it sits flush with the rest of the grass, then scatter a handful of lawn seed over the top so the bare patch fills back in before winter. articles.title: How to actually block AI bots from scraping your website
articles.content: OpenAI , Google, Microsoft and Anthropic have agreed to support a new way for website owners to stop their content being used to train AI models. The companies are backing a shared opt-out signal in a website’s robots.txt file, which tells AI crawlers whether they're allowed to use its content for training. Like a modern day Library of Alexandria, the internet is the single largest source of human knowledge that exists. Countless people have spent their lives cataloguing and uploading the entire history of humanity for the betterment of everyone. AI companies are a tinderbox in this regard. To train and develop better capabilities for their models, AI companies are repeatedly scraping every corner of the internet to create archives of training data. Compounded by changes in search and how people seek information, AI threatens to become the single point of access to information. But just because you have a website, it doesn’t mean you want it constantly scraped by bots stealing your answers to life’s difficult questions so people can access them elsewhere. Luckily, you’re not alone. Outrage from users and website hosts across the internet has been fueled into developing methods to keep AI companies from harvesting data from your websites. Like layering slices of Swiss cheese, these methods work best to keep out scrapers when used in a defense-in-depth manner. But some malicious bots will still find ways to navigate through the holes. Here’s a few ways to keep the honest bots at bay: (Image credit: Shutterstock) 1. Robots.txt This is the crux of OpenAI’s method to honor anti-web scraping markers . The ‘robots.txt’ text file sits in the root directory of your website and provides guidance on how bots should behave. This can be a useful way to provide a digital map to search engine crawlers and can also prevent your site’s servers from becoming overburdened by bot requests. But by adding just a few characters to this file, you can block the majority of bot traffic from accessing your website. Of course, this unfortunately only applies to scrapers that actually abide by the rules of your robots.txt file. OpenAI has set something of a precedent for other AI companies here, adding that, "We encourage other AI providers to honor the signal." There are a few ways to manage which specific bots you would like to allow on your website, but to block AI traffic you can take the following steps: Open your robots.txt file, or create one if you don’t have one using a text editor Add a section to the file using the heading ‘ # AI crawlers ’ To block all AI crawlers, add a line below stating ‘ Disallow: / ’ To block a specific AI crawler, such as ChatGPT, place ‘ User-agent: ChatGPT-User ’ on one line, with ‘ Disallow: / ’ underneath You can prevent AI crawlers from accessing specific pages by adding the web address after the ‘/’. For example, I could stop AI crawlers from accessing my author page by using the rule ‘ Disallow: /author/benedict-collins ’ Update your robots.txt file in the source files of your website 2. User-only viewing Alternatively, you could take the planned Reddit approach to blocking AI traffic by requiring all users to have an account in order to access your website. This is an excellent way to filter out human traffic from bot traffic because user accounts usually need to be verified with an email or phone number - something mostly humans have. But this comes with its own caveats, and Reddit is finding out the hard way in feedback from users. Not requiring an account gives users from all over the web an easier search experience. They can find the information they need without any obstacles, and without handing over personal information to yet another website. Having to log in or create an account to view web content can cause people to ‘bounce’ - they click on your website, see they need to create an account, and immediately back out of your site to seek the information they need elsewhere. articles.title: 3 simple settings to tweak that make your TV picture look instantly better
articles.content: Between toggling game mode on and off, turning on eye comfort shields for late-night viewing, and having native apps constantly override my display choices, my TV picture was looking, frankly, terrible. It is easy to blame a poor streaming bit rate or assume the screen is wearing out, but usually it comes down to a mess of conflicting picture settings fighting each other in the background. After resetting my display and cutting out the clutter, I realized you do not need complicated calibration tools to get things looking right again. Adjusting three specific settings sorted the issue out straight away, bringing back proper brightness, punchy contrast, and natural color. Turn off energy-saving and eco modes (Image: © Tom's Guide / Kaycee Hill ) The first thing holding your screen back is almost certainly an aggressive power-saving mode. Most TVs ship with these turned on by default to meet regional energy efficiency rules, and they can sabotage your picture by capping backlight output or letting an ambient light sensor dim the screen the second you lower the lights in the evening. Head into your TV’s general or picture settings menu, track down Eco Mode or Energy Saving, and switch it off . Disabling it immediately unleashes the panel’s actual peak brightness, making highlights pop and finally giving HDR content the visual punch it is supposed to have. Ditch motion smoothing (Image: © Tom's Guide / Kaycee Hill) If a prestige drama or big-budget action film looks less like cinema and more like a soap opera, motion smoothing is to blame. It's often labelled under names like TruMotion, Picture Clarity, or Motionflow . The mechanism, however, is all the same: the TV artificially inserts fake frames between the real ones to force a hyper-smooth image. While that extra fluidity has its place in live sport, the unnatural effect ruins picture quality. Dive into your picture or clarity settings, find the motion smoothing controls, and turn them off to restore that authentic, cinematic weight to your favourite films and shows. Switch to Filmmaker Mode or Cinema (Image: © Tom's Guide / Kaycee Hill) Out of the box, most sets default to Standard or Vivid mode, which pushes harsh, overly blue whites and neon skin tones designed to catch your eye on a brightly lit shop floor. Swapping your primary preset to Filmmaker Mode or Cinema wipes out that artificial processing with a single press of the remote. Filmmaker Mode disables heavy edge-sharpening filters, strips out fake contrast boosts, and sets the colour temperature to an accurate, industry-standard warm balance. It may look slightly yellow at first while your eyes adjust, but skin tones, shadows, and fine details will quickly look far more natural. articles.title: Open models can do 90 percent of agentic work at a twentieth of the cost of a frontier LLM: Gartner
articles.content: For-profit model-makers, many of which are spending billions on AI infrastructure, will be chasing revenue from just ten percent of steps involved in agentic AI workflows, according to analyst firm Gartner. “Nine in 10 agent workflow steps are routine, and open-weight models handle them at parity for a quarter of the price of the cheapest closed model,” the firm’s senior director Mark Petty and group vice president Raymond Paquet wrote last week in new document titled “Open-Weight Models Will Run 90% of Enterprise Agentic Workflow Steps.” “Typical operational workflows involve hundreds of routine executions, such as classification, tool calling, passing, validating and reconciling data,” the pair observe, before suggesting open-weight models “can handle hundreds of these routine steps for every one that needs frontier reasoning.” “Against the cheapest closed model at the same score, the open model costs a quarter as much. Against a frontier model run on every step, it costs as little as a twentieth,” the pair add. Those are the best-case numbers, because the analysts admit “Current open models can be more verbose and retry more often, so the saving per task against a frontier model is closer to five or six times.” That’s still a lovely saving, but the analysts rate it as the welcome by-product of moving to open models rather than an end in itself. “Years of workflow history are a large part of what an acquirer pays for in a SaaS company and every routine step sent to a frontier API moves a slice of it outside your perimeter,” the pair wrote. “Open-weights preserve your control. The cost saving is a bonus.” The two analysts therefore offer the following strategic planning assumption: “By 2030, 90% of enterprise operational agent workflow steps will execute on open-weight models.” They argue that enterprises will mostly adopt domain-specific open-weight models, because they do well “in scenarios where a small number of highly stable steps run millions of times a month.” Most models, however, are already commodities. Harnesses, the tools that run agents and manage agents, are the source of value in AI products, because one of their roles is to route work to the most appropriate model for a job, without users noticing any impact. A good harness saves money, imposes strong guardrails, and manages agent fleets. Less powerful harnesses leave users with more to do. The paper suggests frontier models will continue to have a role as the engine of research and development and are effectively capital expense. Open-weight models become an operational expense after frontier models do the heavy lifting. ®

articles.title: Here are the 7 biggest upgrades we want to see on Samsung Galaxy S27
articles.content: We're pretty much done for major phone launches in 2026, certainly for devices that will be coming to the U.S. and Europe, which means it's time to start looking forward to what might be coming next year. And, as usual, we expect the first big release of the year to be Samsung's Galaxy S27 series. The S27 series is said to be made up of four phones : The Galaxy S27, Galaxy S27 Plus, Galaxy S27 Ultra and the new Galaxy S27 Pro. We've started hearing some rumors about what those phones could have to offer, including one of the first major redesigns Galaxy phones have had for several years. Obviously there are a few things we also really want to see on these phones as well. So here are the top seven changes we want to see on the Samsung Galaxy S27. Larger silicon carbon batteries (Image credit: Future) Galaxy battery capacity does not change much, if ever. In fact the Galaxy S Ultra batteries have been stuck on the 5,000 mAh plateau since 2020. Meanwhile companies like OnePlus have been offering over 7,000 mAh batteries without any meaningful change to the design. Frankly, people are sick of it, and it's time the Galaxy S27 changed that. Thankfully Samsung has shown that it can do this, thanks to the introduction of silicon carbon batteries in the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series. This technology allows for greater energy density, meaning you can offer more battery capacity without increasing the size of the battery. Rumors suggest this may be happening too, with the S27 Ultra reportedly getting a 5,700 mAh battery. The S27 Pro is tipped to get a 5,200 mAh battery, though we don't know what the S27 and S27 Plus might be getting. We hope they'll get an increase from the 4,300 mAh and 4,900mAh batteries on their S26 counterparts. Magnetic wireless charging (Image credit: Future) One of my biggest gripes with Android phones is how so few of them have adopted the full Qi2 wireless charging standard — complete with the magnetic charging ring. Samsung is one such offender, adding Qi2 charging technology, while relying on special cases to add the magnetic support. Many reasons have been given over the past couple of years, ranging from issues with the S Pen to the fact the camera bump blocks where the magnetic ring should sit. Whatever the reason, it's high time that Samsung got its act together and added Qi2 magnets to its phones, and the S27 series' redesign is the perfect place to do it. A better Privacy Display (Image credit: Samsung) The Privacy Display is one of the best features on the Galaxy S26 Ultra, but it definitely needs some improvements. In particular, Samsung needs to counteract the fact the Privacy Display dims the screen — even when the feature is switched off. Brighter screens offer huge visibility benefits, especially in bright conditions, and that shouldn't be affected by a new screen feature. Especially if you're not actually using it. Similarly viewing angles are also reduced, even when the privacy features are switched off, which is far from ideal. I'd also like to see more control over the Privacy Display and the parts of the screen that are blacked out — rather than letting the phone handle everything automatically. Upgraded camera features (Image credit: @TechHome100) Samsung has a habit of neglecting the camera hardware on some of its phones, particularly the cheaper models like the Galaxy S26 and Galaxy S26 Plus. 50MP main lenses are fine, but 12MP ultrawide and 10MP telephoto lenses aren't befitting a flagship device. It doesn't matter that they don't bear the Ultra branding. At the very least the S27 and S27 Plus need a higher resolution ultrawide lens, ideally something closer to 50MP. Any extra upgrades on the telephoto lens will be a nice bonus. As for the Galaxy S27 Ultra, it's about time we started seeing more advanced camera features. Variable zoom has been rumored for at least a couple of years, and the rumored loss of the secondary telephoto lens feels like the perfect time to offer that. Likewise, now that…

articles.title: OpenAI Introduces Pando: A Git Backend That Cuts Median Push Latency ~80%
articles.content: OpenAI has introduced Pando , a new Git backend that now serves all development in its monorepo. The OpenAI Pando Git backend keeps the standard Git client and protocol. Engineers and Codex agents still run git push and git fetch as before. Only the server changed. OpenAI team reports median push latency fell nearly 80%. Pando now delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. TL;DR Scale: Nearly 1 PB of Git data per day; peak above 57 TB in 1 hour. Runs on: Commodity hardware; standard cloud VMs saturate 10 Gbps links on clone and fetch. Performance: Thousands of concurrent pushers without degradation, per OpenAI’s own testing. Best: Median push latency down nearly 80% (about 5x). Worst: Not open source; repeat branch pushes resend non-trunk history (p99 pack under 3 MiB). What is OpenAI Pando? Pando is a Git-compatible server backend from OpenAI that scales concurrent pushes and fetches for a monorepo. It was written in Rust and reached production in 10 weeks. One engineer designed the core and teams of Codex agents implemented it. It has served production traffic since April 2026. Why did OpenAI need a new Git backend? Codex multiplied parallel work. OpenAI’s commit chart shows commits landed on master up 1,378% in Q3 2026 versus Q1 2024. Its Q4 2026 estimate is +2,442%. Each push now triggers many CI fetches. By late 2025, fetches and pushes slowed, merges failed, and reliability at times fell below 90%. OpenAI concluded the bottleneck was how it served Git, not Git itself. How does Pando work? Pando drops 2 assumptions that most Git servers treat as requirements: 1. Repository-wide consistency : Conventional servers order every ref update repo-wide, so unrelated pushes wait. Pando uses causal consistency instead. Each branch is serialized on its own, and clients only conflict when pushing the same ref. The tradeoff: a reader viewing several branches may see them at different points in time. 2. A unique packfile per client : Standard servers build a fresh pack per fetch. Pando stores each pushed pack as an immutable blob. A “ref version” goes into a scalable metadata store. A push needs O(1) metadata reads and writes. A fetch needs O(log Δ) reads, where Δ is the ref-version gap to close. How are pushes kept small and reusable? With millions of branches, a full ref advertisement can exceed 100 MiB. Pando advertises only the trunk branch as the base for new feature-branch pushes. Any reader with trunk history can then fetch that branch from 1 stored pack. In OpenAI’s monorepo, the median pack was under 20 KiB. How are fetches served at line rate? Pando returns download links via packfile-uri , an existing Git protocol feature. It sends an empty inline pack. A delivery service called Express caches packs regionally, using consistent hashing, with hit rates above 99%. What replaces garbage collection? Each push creates an “L0” pack. Background workers group packs into geometrically larger covers, similar to LSM-tree compaction. The monorepo currently uses covers up to L4. Covers act as a skip list, so pack selection runs in logarithmic time. --> What are the production numbers? All figures below are self-reported by OpenAI. Median push latency reduced by nearly 80%. Nearly 1 PB of Git data per day, using only a handful of CPU cores. Over 57 TB of packs served in a single hour, more than 99% from local disk cache. Clones and fetches saturate 10 Gbps links on standard cloud VMs. OpenAI also ran a 1,000-writer simulation against 3-phase-commit and write-ahead-log designs. It labels these teaching models, not benchmarks. How does Pando compare with other approaches? articles.title: Forget crunches — my physical therapist gave me this exercise to work my abs without aggravating my lower back pain
articles.content: I suffer from sciatica, so I have to be mindful when it comes to ab exercises like crunches and sit-ups, which typically put a lot of stress on the lower back. In the run-up to my last marathon, I asked my physical therapist for an ab exercise that would build core strength and stability without stressing my back — read on to find out what he said next. As a reminder, what works for me might not work for you or your body. If you’re a complete beginner, pregnant or postpartum, or recovering from an injury or surgery, it’s always best to seek personalized advice from a qualified professional. 3 spine-safe exercises for working your core When it comes to a spine-safe way to work your core, the main exercise my therapist recommended is the bird-dog. Read on to find out how to do a bird dog with perfect form, its benefits, plus two other back-friendly exercises to add to your routine. 1. Bird dog (Image credit: Shutterstock) Unlike crunches, which force your back to bend as you lift your head, neck, and shoulders off the mat, bird dog teaches your abdominal muscles to hold your spine in place while your limbs move. This helps build the functional fitness you need for everyday life, as well as during sports like running. As you perform the bird dog, you’ll be working the deep stabilizer muscles that run along the spine and glutes, rather than the outer six-pack muscles. The deep core works as the body’s corset and helps protect your spine from injury. Here’s how to do the bird dog exercise with good form: Start on all fours, with your hands stacked underneath your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Keep your head and spine in a neutral position, so your back and neck are straight. Engage your core, thinking about zipping your abs up and in, and squeezing your belly button into your spine. Slowly, with complete control, extend your right arm straight out in front of you, while also extending your left leg straight back. They should form a straight line with your torso. Pause here for a few seconds, making sure your hips don’t rotate. Imagine there’s a light on each hip — both should be shining down on your mat. Return slowly to your starting position and repeat on the opposite side. Keep alternating until you’ve completed 8-10 reps per side. 2. Dead bug (Image credit: Shutterstock) Another safe exercise to try if you suffer from lower back pain is the dead bug. Again, unlike a crunch or a plank, this exercise targets those all-important deep abdominal muscles while keeping your lower back supported. A huge benefit of the dead bug is that it’s performed lying flat on your back, meaning there is no compressive load on your spinal discs, as you’re not having to fight gravity to hold the pose. This allows you to build core strength and train yourself to maintain a neutral spine without triggering any pain in your lower back. Here’s how to do a dead bug : Lie on your back and raise your arms and legs to a tabletop position: this means your arms are pointing straight up to the ceiling, and your knees are bent at 90 degrees, with your knees in line with your hips. From here, press your lower back into the floor. Engage your core, squeezing your belly button into your spine. Slowly lower your right arm overhead, keeping your arm straight, and at the same time, extend your left leg. Only lower both limbs as low as you can without letting your lower back peel off the floor. Bring both back to your start position and repeat on the opposite side. Keep alternating until you’ve completed 8-10 reps per side. If this is too much for you, start with bent-knee taps. Instead of straightening your leg, keep your knee bent and tap one heel down to the floor, then bring it back to your starting position and repeat on the other side. 3. articles.title: Does AI actually save employees time? Data is contradictory
articles.content: It’s early days for AI-assisted work , and sentiments are mixed about its benefits: Does AI actually bring value and save employees time, or does it bog them down and add unnecessary activities? Data from ActivTrak seems to vacillate between those two potential realities: The latest research from the productivity tracking software company says employees who use AI most heavily are working up to 90 minutes longer each day, yet its previous research, published earlier this year, found that they are actually working less. The discrepancy may be due in part to the timespan and sample sizes of the data collection for the two reports, but it indicates that enterprises should still be wary of vendor claims about AI-related productivity gains. Measuring them remains incredibly difficult. AI use compared ActivTrak’s current findings are based on behavioral work data gathered from 9,140 knowledge workers across 467 enterprises over a five month period (April 1 to September 25, 2026). This sample is much smaller than that of its previous report based on 443 million hours of work performed by 163,638 employees across 1,111 organizations over a three year period (January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2025). According to the latest findings, heavy AI users are working between 8.42 and 9.08 hours per day, compared to 7.58 hours for those not using AI. This contradicts ActivTrak’s previous finding that average workdays had decreased by roughly 9 minutes (a 2% decline) thanks to AI. On the productivity front, heavy AI users have 22% shorter focus sessions than light users (37.8 minutes versus 48.2), suggesting their work is more fragmented due to AI use; further, they switch apps 15% more frequently. “Over time, those interruptions add friction to high-value work that requires concentration, critical thinking, and sustained attention,” Sarah Altemus , manager of the ActivTrak Productivity Lab, said in a blog post describing the latest findings. ActivTrak’s previous report had found that over the period of the earlier study, focus efficiency, the percentage of work time spent in focused, uninterrupted activity, fell to a three year low of 60% with AI use, and average focused session time in 2025 declined by 9% from 2023. However, that same report found that daily productive time increased by 19 minutes, or 5%, to 6 hours and 36 minutes, with AI in the workplace. Furthermore, productive sessions grew by 13%. The company’s latest report also tracked the productivity differences between users of tools with embedded AI and users of web-based AI tools. Those using embedded AI switched apps 0.6 times an hour, while those using AI on the web switched between 1.7 and 4.2 times per hour. That’s up to 4x more switching than by employees who don’t make use of AI at all, which creates what ActivTrak describes as a “swivel-chair tax” — the additional effort spent by employees due to the movement between apps. Similarly, in its previous report, ActivTrak had found that this multitasking rose 12%, or 10-plus minutes, with AI. Interestingly, according to the latest research, light users spend more active work time in core job-specific apps (81.4% compared to 78%). “In other words, more frequent AI engagement doesn’t necessarily translate into more focused work,” Altemus pointed out. The larger issue is the way organizations manage the additional capacity that AI may create , Altemus noted. “When employees complete tasks faster, managers may assume they have room for more responsibilities,” she said. Without clear workload boundaries, time savings may be redirected into additional work that can be taxing. The numbers often don’t tell the full story ActivTrak has a useful view of how work moves across applications, noted Sanchit Vir Gogia , chief analyst at Greyhound Research, but he also pointed out that it sells the capability that produces these measurements. articles.title: 9 top new movies to stream this week on Netflix, Hulu and more (Nov. 3-9)
articles.content: After a couple of quiet weeks, November is starting with a packed slate of new movies across the best streaming services . There’s plenty to watch in the coming days, including new arrivals on Netflix, Hulu, Peacock and AMC+. Plus, there are new picks on premium streaming. Starting with the latter, this week on PVOD you can buy or rent acclaimed movies like “Resident Evil,” “Primetime” and “Bad Apples.” Meanwhile, Netflix debuts its first Christmas movie of the season, and if you're not ready to deck the halls yet, it's also adding an overlooked romantic crime thriller. Alternatively, Hulu has a farcical comedy sequel, and Peacock has a historical action movie starring Andrew Garfield. These are just some of the most noteworthy new movies on streaming this week. Below, I’ve rounded up the highlights to save you from having to scroll through each platform to find out what’s new this week. And don’t forget to check out our guide to the top new TV shows , too. ‘Bad Apples’ (PVOD) Saoirse Ronan stars in this darkly funny thriller that centers on a school teacher pushed to her breaking point by a disruptive pupil. Ronan is the movie’s biggest asset, with the Oscar-nominated actor delivering a strong leading performance. Where the movie stumbles is progressing beyond its initial setup; the middle portion goes through the motions before a finale that takes a big leap in logic. How that swing lands is a matter of personal opinion; it's definitely divisive. Maria Spencer (Ronan) is a good-natured primary school teacher fighting a daily battle with rebellious student Danny (Eddie Waller). When Danny pushes her too far, she impulsively locks him in her basement. At first, she regrets her rash decision. However, when her other students start flourishing in the classroom with Danny’s negative influence removed, she resolves to keep the troublemaker trapped. Watch on Prime Video (buy/rent) starting November 3 ‘Resident Evil’ (PVOD) Director Zach Cregger (“Weapons,” “Barbarian”) delivers the definitive “Resident Evil” movie. The survival horror series has been adapted numerous times. There are the Paul W. S. Anderson movies starring Milla Jovovich, the quickly canceled Netflix series, and several animated efforts, too. None have managed to convey the feeling of playing a Resident Evil video game as well as Cregger’s intense, fast-paced action-horror. Rising star Austin Abrams plays a courier, tasked with delivering vital medical supplies to a remote hospital in the franchise’s iconic Raccoon City. Once on location, he finds the place overrun with mutated creatures. “Resident Evil” does lean a little too heavily on comedy at times, but this is the blockbuster movie the series has long deserved. Watch on Prime Video (buy/rent) starting November 3 ‘Primetime’ (PVOD) 2026 is the year of Robert Pattinson. articles.title: Architect creates open-source replacement for VM migration tool VMware has hidden
articles.content: A cloud architect has created an open-source alternative to VMware’s Virtual Disk Development Kit (VDDK), which the virtualization giant recently withdrew from public downloads. VMware describes VDDK as “a set of libraries and utilities that enable software developers to create applications that can access and manipulate virtual disks” and “a valuable tool for developers of storage and backup applications.” Users, along with VMware’s rivals, had another use for VDDK: migrating VMs to alternative virtualization platforms. In August, VMware restricted access to VDDK downloads to its partners, meaning VMware customers couldn’t access the tool and some of its rivals’ migration tools became less effective. Cloud architect Andrija Panić decided to do something about it. “Many tools that have nothing in common except VMware use the same small library to read a virtual machine’s disks: virt-v2v and nbdkit, the importers in Forklift/MTV, Proxmox VE and Apache CloudStack, and countless in-house scripts,” he told The Register by email. “When public VDDK downloads ended, all of them became harder to install and run.” “I didn’t think it was fair that people’s ability to move or protect their own data should depend on a download page.” He describes the project as “an independent drop-in for libvixDiskLib.so.8.0.3, the disk library that VMware backup and migration tools load to read virtual disks. It was written from scratch, using only public documentation and black-box testing, and contains no VMware code.” Panić told The Register he wrote the tool in Go, with a thin C layer that exposes exactly the same C interface, library name and symbol versions as VMware’s code. The tool cannot write disks, just read them for backup and migration purposes. In his email to The Register , Panić said he has successfully tested OpenVDDK on vSphere versions 6.7 U3, 7.0.3, 8.0.3, 9.1.1. He said that tests in his lab with the latter version, accessing OpenVDDK through vCenter on a standalone ESXi host, saw every disk read match. “Independent testers have reported successful use with Forklift (VMware to KubeVirt, cold and warm), MTV on OpenShift (cold and warm), a Proxmox VE pipeline and custom nbdkit-based tools,” the architect told The Register . “I've received reports of production use, including a German cloud provider migrating a large file server with V2K Migrate and a US-based company migrating to Apache CloudStack/KVM.” Panić was at pains to point out that the reports of successful use are “not independently audited customer endorsements or a guarantee of suitability for every production environment.” As is often the case with FOSS tools. OpenVDDK is not the only option for migrating away from VMware without VDDK. KVM-based OpenNebula has a tool called OneSwap that it says has a 96 percent success rate. Nutanix recently tweaked its “Move” migration tool so it can do the job without VDDK. Red Hat is working on a fix but has provided details of a workaround . Panić made OpenVDDK available under an Apache license, so perhaps Red Hat and others will find it useful as they re-jig their VM migration tools. ®

articles.title: Here’s who is falling in line for Trump’s “Super Intelligence” loyalty test
articles.content: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here . At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order that contained just one directive, ordering government agencies to rebrand what they had been calling artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence.” That term beat out other contenders, including “Extreme Intelligence” and “Supreme Intelligence,” offered by the president in a poll on X a couple of weeks earlier. Rebrands are, of course, now a White House tradition: Trump has changed names to project US dominance of certain bodies of water (the Gulf of America and Lake America), to signal new institutional priorities (Department of War), or simply to leave his mark on storied places (see the ongoing fight over renaming the Kennedy Center). The stated reason for this name change is that today’s AI systems “amplify human ingenuity” rather than merely “imitate” intelligence, and the government’s terminology should reflect that. But if this rebrand follows the pattern of others, its effects will extend beyond government. It will turn a choice of words into a political loyalty test: Those who use the new term demonstrate allegiance to the administration, and those who don’t become marks for attacks (recall that the Trump administration barred the Associated Press from some White House press events after the news outlet did not adopt the term “Gulf of America”). But most Americans go months without ever pondering what to call the major lake between New York and Canada. AI, on the other hand, is at the center of our national conversation and a technology two-thirds of Americans report interacting with multiple times a week. It might be the boldest rebrand yet. So one month in, who’s on board? Let’s start with the government itself. The term “Super Intelligence”—or simply “SI”—now appears more often on government solicitations, like a new request by Immigration and Customs Enforcement for companies to build “SI-powered” surveillance for ICE detention facilities. The new term has been swapped in silently on most government websites. Some, including that of the National Institutes of Health, now include a banner warning visitors they might see both the new and the old terms during the transition period. There have been hiccups. A day after the rebrand order, the Pentagon announced an ambitious new initiative to study the future of warfare, called Project Meridian; it used the old terminology. A Federal Trade Commission press release last week used “superintelligence” instead of the two-word, capitalized version ordered by the president, and recent press releases from Health and Human Services show no sign of the new language. The term “AI” will likely stick around given the countless AI-related offices, initiatives, and programs that have sprung up in recent years, like the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office at the Pentagon (the executive order says it doesn’t apply to previously issued regulations or documents). As for government employees, it appears to be taking time for “SI” rather than “AI” to roll off the tongue. One researcher at a national lab I interviewed a few weeks ago used “AI” repeatedly before sheepishly acknowledging the slip-up. Even Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used “AI” in an interview on October 3. But Trump’s other rebrands suggest the goal isn’t merely to change the government’s vocabulary. It’s to change how the rest of us speak, too. In the past couple of weeks, most of President Trump’s posts on Truth Social have been endorsements for candidates in the midterms. But on October 27 he took a break from electioneering to criticize the Wall Street Journal for not using “Super Intelligence,” “the name which virtually everyone else is using, or soon will be.” He suggested that a new rule will soon go further than the executive order to outright ban “artificial intelligence” from government…

articles.title: Toyota shows off SoC that stores model weights and its OS on integrated memory
articles.content: Japanese carmaker -maker Toyota has decided to have a crack at the market for AI processors. Toyota is the major shareholder in a company called AISIN, a manufacturer of automotive components. Both companies are aware that cars are increasingly reliant on tech like image recognition, and that robotics and other forms of “physical AI” will need parts that overlap with cars. AISIN thinks existing chips aren’t a good fit for such roles, because they rely on external memory to store AI models and then generate a lot of traffic between a processor and the model. That traffic, the company contends, makes image recognition and other on-device uses of AI less effective. DRAM is also currently vastly expensive. The company’s response is a system-on-chip built on a 16nm FinFET process, an Arm Cortex A53 dual-core CPU, plus an Arm MaliG31 GPU. The chip includes built-in STT-MRAM, which stores both model weights and an operating system. AISIN and its research partners at Tohoku University say that approach means the chip can go from power-on to kernel startup in 65.7 milliseconds – 38 times faster than is possible if using external memory – and run the Tiny YOLOv3 object detection algorithm on the chip. “To effectively utilize the limited on-chip memory capacity, a hybrid multiplication architecture combining 8-bit and 16-bit multiplication was developed” according to a machine translation of Tohoku University’s announcement [PDF]. “By combining 16x16, 16x8, and 8x8 bit multiplication, the amount of weight data for the AI model was reduced by 53 percent, from 17.7MB to 9.36MB, while maintaining 16-bit precision.” AISIN is an established parts supplier and already sells to Toyota and other automakers but hasn’t said if or when it can get this chip into production. Meanwhile, the likes of Nvidia and Qualcomm very much want to sell their silicon to carmakers, and position themselves as sources of tech and AI smarts that existing automotive supply chain participants can’t match. ®

articles.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
articles.content: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user’s Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet’s access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines. A report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said Google has severed ties with Videostrong Technology Co. , a TV box manufacturer in China that GTIG and other industry experts concluded was responsible for including malware that enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in a botnet dubbed “ XCPE ” (named after one of the malware’s core code components). The global distribution of XCPE botnet infections. Image: Google Threat Intelligence Group. The report said the XCPE botnet loaded the user’s device with software that makes their Internet address available for resale by multiple “residential proxy” services, which allow customers to rent Internet addresses as a way to anonymize their web traffic or spoof their true location. As detailed in several stories here over the past year , residential proxy services are a major source of unwanted and often malicious traffic, including account takeover activity, advertising fraud, and mass content scraping for AI projects. “Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices,” the GTIG post reads, noting that Google took legal action to take down the domains and servers Videostrong used to control the botnet and install additional malware. “A device manufacturer intentionally infecting their users with malware is an unacceptable breach of trust, and represents a serious risk to those users. Without users’ knowledge or consent, infected devices were offered as a distribution mechanism for a wide array of criminal actors.” The report notes that while TV boxes made up the the majority of the botnet, the same XCPE malware was found in other Android-based IoT products, including telehealth devices, karaoke machines, and even digital signage systems . Google said it requires all Android device makers to pass compatibility and security tests to ensure their products don’t harm users, but that Videostrong nevertheless found a way to load their malicious software immediately after a user boots up one of these devices for the first time (Google says it has since addressed that weakness). The GTIG report calls out a number of residential proxy providers whose software development kits were routinely downloaded by devices infected by the XCPE botnet. Those include AppSalt , also known as Honeygain , which is owned by the Vilnius, Lithuania-based Oxylabs . In October 2026, Oxylabs was relaunched under a new brand called Source , after receiving $130 million in funding from private equity firm Warburg Pincus that reportedly valued the business at $3.6 billion. Oxylabs did not respond to a request for comment. Another provider linked to the botnet was NetNut , a once sprawling residential proxy company operated by the publicly-traded Israeli company Alarum Technologies . In July 2026, the FBI worked with industry partners to seize hundreds of domains associated with NetNut , saying the company was responsible for operating a separate botnet called Popa that enslaved TV boxes as residential proxies. Other proxy providers named in the GTIG report include EarnFM , Traffmonetizer , Jaguar , LINKFOG , BMW/IPWeb and GaGaNode . articles.title: Palantir cofounder wants a 30,000 monkey farm in the US — because AI jacked up macaque prices by 700% in seven years
articles.content: Rapid drug discovery using AI's assistance is adding pressure to an already restricted macaque supply A US startup plans to breed 30,000 monkeys over two decades China's export ban cut off a major source of American research animals Artificial intelligence is creating new demands for pharmaceutical research, increasing pressure on all kinds of resources needed to develop and test potential treatments - including animal test subjects. Macaques, commonly used in medical experiments, have become considerably more expensive, with reported prices rising from approximately $3,000 in 2019 to more than $20,000 today. Now , Palantir cofounder Joe Lonsdale is reportedly supporting Safer Human Medicine, a startup seeking to establish a large-scale breeding facility in the US. Rising demand meets restricted monkey supplies The proposed facility would eventually accommodate 30,000 monkeys, with the company planning to increase its breeding population gradually over approximately 20 years. Its initial stock would comprise between 500 and 1,000 macaques obtained from breeding facilities across Asia. The company intends to expand domestic production and reduce American laboratories’ dependence on imported animals for pharmaceutical research and testing. Artificial intelligence has intensified the pressure by enabling researchers to develop potential medicines more rapidly and generate more drug candidates for testing. Each promising candidate may then require laboratory studies to assess toxicity, safety and biological effects before human clinical trials. Some experimental treatments require animal studies before human trials, and macaques are frequently selected because of their biological similarities to humans. However, the supply problem predates the recent expansion of artificial intelligence applications within pharmaceutical research and drug discovery programmes. China, previously responsible for approximately 60% of America's laboratory monkey imports, prohibited exports in 2020, forcing researchers to seek alternative suppliers. American laboratories subsequently turned to Cambodia, but investigations in 2022 uncovered allegations involving wild-caught monkeys falsely represented as captive-bred animals. Breeding limitations and animal welfare concerns Expanding captive populations is not an immediate solution because female macaques generally reach reproductive maturity around four years of age. Each female typically produces one offspring annually, limiting how quickly breeding operations can increase their populations to meet laboratory requirements. China now reportedly charges approximately $26,000 per macaque, roughly nine times the price recorded in 2019. American laboratories reportedly import approximately 20,000 monkeys annually, leaving researchers exposed to international supply restrictions and substantial procurement expenses. Safer Human Medicine's proposed operation would therefore require considerable time before its intended population could supply a significant share of domestic demand. Nevertheless, the plan has already attracted criticism from animal welfare advocates concerned about keeping thousands of primates for experimental purposes. A critic on X described the proposed breeding operation as “morally indefensible,” and others have called for judicial intervention against what they consider animal abuse. Their objections could lead to legal challenges, potentially delaying construction, breeding activities, or the company's plans to establish domestic production capacity. The eventual progress of this project will depend not only on breeding capacity and commercial demand, but also on regulatory scrutiny and potential court proceedings. Via Ole Lehmann on X

articles.title: Zyphra AI Introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA): A Path to True Subquadratic Attention
articles.content:
Zyphra has released Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA) , a sparse attention method built around a tree-structured indexer. ZHA targets a known gap in sparse attention: the indexer that picks tokens still scans the whole context. Zyphra’s technical paper shows ZHA can be distilled into frozen pretrained models with about 4B tokens. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B it stays close to dense attention on reasoning, agentic coding and 256K retrieval benchmarks. TL;DR Size: It is a method that adds 81,920 trainable parameters to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (about 0.00024%). Tested up to 256K context. Runs on: Retrofits frozen pretrained models after a 4B-token KL warmup at 32K context. Speedups come from a modeled H100 BF16 roofline. No optimized kernels released. An FP4 router variant was also tested. Performance: Within a few points of dense attention on 7 reasoning, coding and retrieval benchmarks. Best: LongBench v2 hits 63.4% (deep tree) vs 58.0% dense, using about 1.1% of keys. Worst: On NoPE-based Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B, deep-tree RULER-13 drops 25.3 points below dense. What is Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA)? ZHA is a sparse attention method from Zyphra that finds relevant keys by searching a tree. It keeps the full KV cache. The tree only decides which cached keys each query reads. Fixed-state methods like SSMs and sliding windows saturate at long contexts. Fine-grained sparse methods like DeepSeek Sparse Attention score every past token with an indexer. The final attention is sparse, but the indexer still grows with the full context. Near 1M tokens, cited work shows indexing takes 60 to 90% of layer time. ZHA makes the search itself sparse. How does ZHA’s tree indexer work? Building the tree ZHA splits keys into contiguous chunks and compresses each chunk into a summary key. Summaries are grouped and compressed again, level by level. With chunk size 4, 6 levels cover 4,096 tokens per top node. Summaries come from a small set of learned reference queries . Each reference query gives a tangent-plane estimate of a chunk’s log attention mass. The max over these planes approximates how much attention any future query would give the chunk. How does top-p routing pick tokens? At decode time, a query scores the top-level nodes. It keeps the smallest set holding a fraction p of estimated attention mass. It then expands only those children, repeating until it reaches raw KV entries. Top-p makes the budget adaptive. A single-fact lookup touches few branches. A query that needs many scattered facts expands more. The first token is always kept as an attention sink. How does ZHA perform against dense attention and MSA? Zyphra team converted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with 2 trees: deep (chunk 4, 6 levels) and wide (chunk 256, 1 level). Both use 16 reference queries and p = 0.95. It also trained a MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) indexer on 40B tokens, 10x ZHA’s budget. Benchmark (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) Dense ZHA deep ZHA wide MSA AIME 2026 93.1 91.2 90.8 91.7 SWE-bench Verified 67.4 67.4 68.4 63.6 Terminal-Bench 2.1 49.9 46.7 53.3 46.1 MMLU-Pro 84.9 85.3 85.2 85.3 GPQA Diamond 84.8 85.0 85.0 83.1 RULER-13 (256K) 96.0 93.3 96.2 77.1 LongBench v2 (thinking) 58.0 63.4 62.4 49.3 Source: arXiv 2610.42112 , Figure 5. All numbers self-reported by Zyphra. The biggest gap is on retrieval. MSA drops to 77.1% on RULER-13, while both ZHA trees stay above 93%. On LongBench v2, the deep tree and MSA read similar key shares (1.1% vs 1%). The deep tree scores 14.1 points higher. Across 28 tree geometries, RULER accuracy held steady when attending to 10 to 30% of keys. At fixed compression, deeper trees kept accuracy at higher sparsity. A 4-parameter model predicts RULER accuracy from geometry with 1.44-point RMSE. Back

articles.titleFa: معرفی روش توجه سلسله‌مراتبی Zyphra AI: مسیر رسیدن به توجه زیرنسبتی واقعی
articles.summaryFa: Zyphra یک روش جدید به نام توجه سلسله‌مراتبی Zyphra (ZHA) را معرفی کرده که بر پایه‌ی یک ایندکس‌گر مبتنی بر درخت استوار است. این روش به طور خاص بر خلاء موجود در توجه‌های اسپارس تمرکز دارد و می‌تواند به مدل‌های پری‌تریند یخ‌زده با حدود ۴ میلیارد توکن فشرده شود. ZHA در معیارهای استدلال، کدنویسی و جستجو از توجه متراکم نزدیک است و به بهبود عملکرد مدل‌های بزرگ کمک می‌کند.
articles.summaryEn: Zyphra has introduced a new method called Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), which is based on a tree-structured indexer and addresses a gap in sparse attention. This method can be distilled into frozen pretrained models with around 4 billion tokens and performs closely to dense attention on reasoning, coding, and retrieval benchmarks, thus enhancing the performance of large models.

articles.title: Apple Requiring Developers to Disclose Location Sharing and Dating Features in Apps
articles.content: Starting November 16, Apple will require developers to disclose whether their apps include real-world location sharing or dating features so age ratings can be assigned appropriately. Apple says the Dating and Relationships disclosure is required for apps that allow dating or relationship connections, regardless of whether that's with a real person or a virtual companion that engages in sexual or romantic content. Apps that include Dating and Relationships must have a minimum age rating of 18+, but Shared Location apps may not see a change to their minimum age rating in some regions. In Brazil, apps are required to have an A16 rating for Shared Location and A18 for Dating and Relationships. Apps that may qualify for a lower age rating, such as an app that offers location sharing for parents and children, can request a rating from Brazil's Ministry of Justice and Public Security. Apps must have Shared Location and Dating and Relationships disclosures submitted through App Store Connect by January 12, 2027.
